sense: keep to, not violate (a rule, a right, someone’s wishes)

terms.gloss: keep, comply with, respect (a law, a rule, an agreement)
evidence: Cic. Off. 2.40: lēgēs latrōnum esse dīcuntur, quibus pāreant, quās observent
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “to observe, respect, regard, attend to, heed, keep, comply with a law, precept, recommendation, etc.” For respect for a person see respect (esteem).

terms.gloss: have regard for, take into account (others, their interests)
evidence: Cic. Off. 1.139: habenda ratiō nōn sua sōlum, sed etiam aliōrum

terms.gloss: respect for others’ feelings, consideration; modesty
evidence: Cic. Off. 1.99: jūstitiae partēs sunt nōn violāre hominēs, verēcundiae nōn offendere
terms.comment: With a genitive, “respect for”: lēgum, for the laws (Liv. 10.13.8, Lewis & Short). The opposite of respecting a law or a person is violāre.

phrases.latin: Quīn etiam lēgēs latrōnum esse dīcuntur, quibus pāreant, quās observent.
phrases.english: Why, even robbers are said to have laws that they obey and respect.

phrases.latin: est autem quod differat in hominum ratiōne habendā inter jūstitiam et verēcundiam. Jūstitiae partēs sunt nōn violāre hominēs, verēcundiae nōn offendere
phrases.english: But in the regard we pay to people, justice and respect differ: it is the part of justice not to wrong people, of respect not to offend them

phrases.latin: ut in cēterīs habenda ratiō nōn sua sōlum, sed etiam aliōrum
phrases.english: as in everything else, one must have regard not only for oneself but for others too

sources: Lewis & Short: observo · Lewis & Short: ratio · Lewis & Short: verecundia
Cicero, De officiis 1 and 2, checked against the Latin Library texts (CLTK mirror) (9 November 2026).
